clue.text: Hard worker never finishing — a Bulgarian maybe

indicators.note: never finishing says the word for the worker stops short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a slave is someone forced to toil hard

explanation.surface: A hard-working Bulgarian who never gets to the end of the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'never finishing' removes the last letter E from SLAVE. Bulgarians are a South Slavic people, so 'maybe' marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Bulgarians belong to the Slavic family of peoples, so a Bulgarian is one example of that ethnic group.

clue.text: Uninteresting rubbish that can give householder problem

parts.note: dry means dull or uninteresting, as a dry lecture
rot means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: Something dull and worthless that ends up causing trouble for a homeowner.
explanation.definitionFit: This fungal decay of timber in buildings is a classic and costly headache for people who own a house.

clue.text: It may make one look up to ancestors

definitions.text: It may make one look up to ancestors

parts.words: It may make one look up to ancestors
parts.note: read literally, 'look up to' is admire; cryptically, a lineage chart is read upward from oneself toward earlier generations

explanation.surface: Something that makes a person respect their forebears.
explanation.definitionFit: A genealogical chart puts forebears above descendants, so tracing your line means reading upward from yourself.

clue.text: Wood and seaweed on the beach

parts.note: ash is a tree and the timber it gives
ore is an old word for seaweed, as in oarweed

explanation.surface: Driftwood and seaweed lying on the sand.
explanation.walkthrough: ORE meaning seaweed is a dictionary word chiefly met in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on land at the shore's edge rather than at sea is to be on the beach.

clue.text: Attractive English silver at home, Georgian primarily

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
in means at home, as in 'staying in'

indicators.note: primarily asks for the first letter of the word Georgian before it

explanation.surface: Praising a charming English silver collection kept at home, mostly Georgian pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something charming that draws people in is appealing, a close synonym.

clue.text: County hospital's basic requirements?

definitions.meaning: the usual short form of Bedfordshire, a county north of London
places for patients to lie down are the most basic thing a hospital provides

explanation.definitionFit: Bedfordshire is shortened in addresses to this form, and a ward's fundamental fittings are the cots patients sleep in.

clue.text: Old politician with awfully trite words on stage

parts.note: Lib is short for a member of the old Liberal party in Britain

indicators.note: awfully suggests the word trite is badly mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A veteran politician spouting dreadfully clichéd lines at a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old politician' suggests a statesman, but it is the abbreviation for a member of the Liberal party, Britain's main centre party before the Liberal Democrats; 'awfully' scrambles TRITE.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the texts of operas, the sung words performed in a theatre production.

clue.text: Edinburgh medic could treat anyone with cold

indicators.note: to treat something is to work on it, so the letters of these words get reshaped

explanation.surface: A doctor from Scotland's capital able to cure anybody's sniffles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could treat' rearranges the letters of ANYONE and COLD together. The creator of Sherlock Holmes trained as a doctor at Edinburgh University.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sherlock Holmes author qualified as a physician at Edinburgh University and practised medicine before writing full time.

clue.text: Look, sailors, a girl!

parts.note: lo is an old exclamation meaning look or behold
RN, the Royal Navy, stands for sailors

explanation.surface: A naval crew pointing out a young woman on shore.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a female first name, made famous by the romantic novel about Exmoor.

clue.text: A bonnet is inappropriate as garment for the condemned

indicators.note: inappropriate suggests the letters are out of their proper place, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fashion verdict that a bonnet is unsuitable clothing for someone about to be executed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inappropriate' rearranges the letters of A BONNET IS; 'as' links fodder to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This yellow penitential tunic was worn by heretics sentenced by the Spanish Inquisition at an auto-da-fé.

clue.text: Unpleasant sensation — I turn green at first

indicators.note: at first moves the colour word green to the front, ahead of the other pieces

parts.note: vert is the heraldic term for green
a go is a turn, as in 'your go'

explanation.surface: Someone feeling queasy says they are going green.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'I turn green' as feeling sick, which is apt; VERT, the heraldic word for green, is a crossword staple, and 'at first' moves it ahead of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Dizziness, a spinning feeling often brought on by heights, is a disagreeable bodily sensation.

clue.text: Gangster expelled by one country and another

indicators.note: expelled by says the gangster is thrown out of the country named next

parts.note: Australia is a country
Al Capone, the Chicago gangster, gives his first name

explanation.surface: A mobster deported from one nation and then another.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing AL from AUSTRALIA leaves a different country, so 'another' (country) is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Central European state, so it is a second country beside the one named in the wordplay.

clue.text: Friendly mum still coming round

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother

indicators.note: coming round says the word for still is turned about, read backwards

parts.note: yet means still, as in 'yet more'

explanation.surface: A warm-hearted mother who still pays visits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still coming round' reads as a visiting mother; 'coming round' is the reversal signal applied to the word for still.
explanation.definitionFit: Pally and sociable; the colloquial adjective from 'mate' means friendly.

clue.text: It's one on the threshold of breaking the sound barrier

definitions.text: It's one on the threshold of breaking the sound barrier

parts.words: It's one on the threshold of breaking the sound barrier
parts.note: the speed ratio that measures how fast an aircraft flies against sound reaches one exactly as it goes supersonic

explanation.surface: Describing something poised to go faster than sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The ratio of an object's speed to the speed of sound equals one exactly at the supersonic threshold.

clue.text: Reg made it abroad — having done this?

definitions.text: Reg made it abroad — having done this?

indicators.note: abroad here means scattered widely, so the letters of these words are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A man named Reg succeeded overseas, presumably after moving there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' rearranges REG MADE IT, and the whole clue describes someone who made it abroad after leaving home.
explanation.definitionFit: Having moved away from one's own country to settle in another is what someone who made it overseas has done.

clue.text: Restoring confidence with silly grins — a ruse

indicators.note: silly suggests these letters are in a foolish jumble and must be sorted out

explanation.surface: Comforting someone with foolish smiles that are only a trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' rearranges the letters of GRINS and A RUSE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Comforting words that remove doubt are those that give back a person's faith in things.

clue.text: 'Fatty' recovering after treatment — what's the point of all that weight?

definitions.text: what's the point of all that weight?

indicators.note: after treatment suggests the letters have been worked on and come out rearranged

explanation.surface: An overweight patient recovering after medical care wonders what all that bulk was for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after treatment' rearranges the letters of FATTY RECOVERING.
explanation.definitionFit: Physics defines the single point through which a body's entire weight can be taken to act.

clue.text: Name male in 12 in short communication

indicators.note: the second in places the male, in and code letters inside the word for a message

parts.note: a note is a brief written message
taken as written
12 refers to the country at 12 across, whose international vehicle code is A

explanation.surface: Naming a man in a Central European country by brief message.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's '12' points to 12 across, whose international vehicle registration letter is A.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone forward for a post or award is to propose them by naming them.

clue.text: One trail winding perhaps from china

indicators.note: winding suggests a twisting path, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A single meandering path, possibly porcelain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winding' rearranges ONE TRAIL. The lower-case 'china' disguises the country China.
explanation.definitionFit: Something from the Far East, such as China, is described as Eastern in origin.

clue.text: Adding certain characters to dull English clique

parts.note: numb means deadened or dulled in feeling
a ring is a close group or clique, as in a spy ring

explanation.surface: Introducing particular letters to a tedious English group.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing figures against items, like pages or seats, is adding digits, which are a kind of character.

clue.text: Senior lady with two names embraced by poet

indicators.note: embraced by says the two names sit inside the poet's name

parts.note: Thomas Gray, author of the Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard
N is the abbreviation for name, so two names give two Ns

explanation.surface: An elderly woman with a double-barrelled name hugged by a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: N for name is a dictionary abbreviation; 'embraced by' sets the pair inside the surname of Thomas Gray, the 18th-century English poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandmother is an older woman of the family, affectionately a senior lady.

clue.text: Novelist to launch forth audibly

indicators.note: audibly asks for a word that sounds like the launch word, rather than one spelt the same

parts.note: to shoot is to launch forth, as an arrow or rocket

explanation.surface: A writer about to burst out loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: Nevil Shute wrote A Town Like Alice and On the Beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Nevil Shute was an English-born writer of popular fiction such as A Town Like Alice.

clue.text: Complete agreement — boy should go to higher education establishment

indicators.note: should go to places the boy after the university, as if he is sent there

parts.note: uni is a short word for university
a son is a boy child

explanation.surface: Everyone agrees the lad ought to go to university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should go to' reads as advice about the boy's education, but it places the boy after the university word in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing or saying something all together in perfect accord is acting as one voice.

clue.text: One fellow cross with another bloke on the island

parts.note: a man is a fellow
X is a cross shape
another means one more fellow, a second man

explanation.surface: A man gets annoyed with another man somewhere on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like an adjective meaning angry; it is the letter X. The island is the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Isle of Man is a male islander, a bloke from that island.

clue.text: Saint making an impression

definitions.meaning: the evangelist who wrote the second gospel
a dent or stain left on a surface

explanation.definitionFit: One of the four gospel writers, and also a trace or imprint left on something.

clue.text: Duration of broadcast? I'm irate when it's changed

indicators.note: when it's changed says the letters of the phrase before are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: An angry listener complains whenever the broadcast schedule is altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when it's changed' rearranges the letters of I'M IRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: The time allotted to a programme or speaker on radio or television is its broadcasting length.

clue.text: Looks at three in bikinis reportedly!

indicators.note: reportedly asks for a word that sounds like the plural letter, not one spelt the same

parts.note: the word bikinis contains three of the letter I, so three of them are the plural of that letter

explanation.surface: Ogling a trio of women in swimwear.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural of the letter I, said aloud, matches the verb. The surface invites a leering picture, but 'three' counts letters in the word bikinis.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye something is to watch or gaze at it, so the third-person verb means looks at.

clue.text: Give consideration to part of hospital? Sure, with a hundred leaving!

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

indicators.note: leaving says the hundred goes out of the word for sure

parts.note: certain means sure
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Asking whether a hospital department should be considered, with confidence once a hundred patients have gone.
explanation.walkthrough: ENT (ear, nose and throat) is a standard hospital department; 'leaving' removes the Roman hundred from the word for sure.
explanation.definitionFit: To entertain an idea or offer is to consider it seriously.

clue.text: Stony female favoured returning gong

indicators.note: returning says the word for favoured comes back, read backwards

parts.note: in means favoured or popular, as in 'in with the crowd'
a gong is British slang for a medal or honour, here the OBE, Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted woman who got a medal coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses IN into NI. In Greek myth this mother wept for her slain children until she was turned to stone.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the grieving mother was transformed into a rock that still weeps, making her a woman of stone.
